q: 1. The commonly used material in the manufacture of cement is
explain: Lime stone (calcareous material) supplies the required lime (CaO) content, which forms the major ingredient of cement, hence it is the commonly used raw material.

q: 2. To obtain cement dry powder, lime stones and shales or their slurry, is burnt in a rotary kiln at a temperature between
explain: In the rotary kiln, the raw mix is burnt at 1400°C–1500°C, the clinkering temperature, at which the raw materials fuse to form cement clinker.

q: 3. How much cement contained in one bag
explain: A standard bag of cement weighs 50 kg, which corresponds to a weight (force) of about 500 N (50 × 9.81 ≈ 490.5 N ≈ 500 N).

q: 4. The maximum quantity of ingredients present in cement production is
explain: Lime (CaO) forms the largest proportion (about 60-65%) of the chemical composition of cement, hence it is present in maximum quantity.

q: 5. The minimum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is
explain: Iron oxide is present in the smallest percentage (about 3-4%) among the major ingredients (lime, silica, alumina, iron oxide) of cement.

q: 6. The minimum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
explain: Magnesium oxide is a minor constituent and is present in the least percentage (about 1-3%) among all chemical ingredients of cement; its excess makes cement unsound.

q: 7. Pick up the correct proportions of chemical ingredients of cement
explain: The typical proportion of ingredients in cement is Lime 63%, Silica 22%, Alumina 6%, and Iron oxide 3%.

q: 8. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: lime in excess, causes the cement to expand and disintegrate
silica in excess, causes the cement to set slowly
alumina in excess, reduces the strength of the cement
magnesium oxide in excess, remains in free state and makes the cement unsound
explain: All the listed effects of excess lime, silica, alumina, and magnesium oxide are correct statements regarding their influence on cement properties.

q: 9. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to an excess of
explain: Excess alkalis in cement react with atmospheric moisture and carbon dioxide, forming soluble salts that migrate to the surface, causing efflorescence (white deposits).

q: 10. An ordinary Portland cement when tested for its fineness, should not leave any residue on I.S sieve No 9 more than
explain: As per IS specifications, the residue retained on IS sieve No. 9 (90 micron) should not exceed 10% for ordinary Portland cement, ensuring adequate fineness.

q: 11. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following :
options: gypsum in cement decreases the setting time
the first compound of cement which reacts with water, is C2S
bulking of sand is less when its particles are fine
explain: All three statements are actually incorrect: gypsum increases (not decreases) setting time, C3A (not C2S) reacts first with water, and bulking of sand is more (not less) when particles are fine. Hence 'all of the above' is the correct choice for incorrect statements.

q: 12. Cement used for normal concrete construction, is obtained by burning a mixture of
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured by burning a mixture of silicious, argillaceous (clayey), and calcareous (limestone) materials together.

q: 13. The mixture of different ingredients of cement, is burnt at
explain: The raw mixture of cement ingredients is burnt at approximately 1400°C, the clinkering temperature, to form cement clinker.

q: 14. The cement whose strength is little lower than the ordinary cement during the first three months but attains afterwards the same strength, is known as
explain: Low-heat Portland cement develops strength slowly at early stages due to lower C3S and C3A content, but eventually catches up with the strength of ordinary cement after about three months.

q: 15. For construction of structures in sea water, the cement generally preferred to, is
explain: Portland pozzolana cement is preferred in sea water construction as it has better resistance to sulphate attack and lower permeability, reducing chemical attack from sea water.

q: 16. For quality control of portland cement, the test essentially done is
explain: Quality control of Portland cement requires testing setting time, soundness, tensile/compressive strength, and consistency, hence all of these are essential.

q: 17. Sieve analysis of portland cement is performed on IS sieve No.
explain: Fineness of Portland cement is tested by sieving on IS Sieve No. 9 (90 micron sieve) as per Indian Standard specifications.

q: 18. During manufacturing process of portland cement, gypsum or plaster of paris is added
options: to increase the strength of cement
to modify the colour of cement
to adjust the setting time of cement
explain: Gypsum is added to cement clinker to control/retard the fast setting action of tricalcium aluminate (C3A), thereby adjusting the setting time of cement.

q: 19. The percentage of gypsum added to the clinker during manufacturing process is
explain: Gypsum is typically added in the range of 0.35% to 5.0% by weight of clinker to regulate the setting time of cement.

q: 20. Addition of sugar in concrete results in
options: increase in setting time by about 1 hr
increase in setting time by about 4 hr
decrease in setting time by about 1 hr
decrease in setting time by about 4 hr
explain: Sugar acts as a retarder in concrete; it delays the setting time significantly, by about 4 hours, when added in small quantities.

q: 21. Setting time of cement decreases by adding
explain: Calcium chloride acts as an accelerator, speeding up the hydration reaction and thereby decreasing the setting time of cement.

q: 22. The minimum initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement is
explain: As per IS code, the minimum initial setting time specified for ordinary Portland cement is 30 minutes.

q: 23. Addition of pozzolana to ordinary portland cement, causes
options: reduction in chemical action with sulphates
explain: Addition of pozzolana affects cement in all these ways: it lowers early strength, reduces sulphate attack, increases shrinkage slightly, and reduces bleeding, hence all statements are correct.

q: 24. Addition of pozzolana to cement
explain: Pozzolana actually increases workability, may reduce ultimate strength contribution initially, decreases heat of hydration, and requires longer curing — so none of the listed options are correct.

q: 25. Pozzolana cement is used with confidence for
explain: Due to its low heat of hydration and resistance to chemical attack, pozzolana cement is confidently used in dams, massive foundations, abutments, and RCC structures.

q: 26. Slag cement is used is
explain: Slag cement, having moderate heat of hydration and good resistance properties, is commonly used for abutments among the given options.

q: 27. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: insufficient quantity of water makes the concrete mix harsh
insufficient quantity of water makes the concrete unworkable
excess quantity of water makes the concrete mix segregated
excess quantity of water cause bleeding in concrete
explain: All these statements about the effect of water quantity (deficiency causing harshness/unworkability, excess causing segregation/bleeding) on concrete are correct.

q: 28. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) generates more heat of hydration
Tricalcium silicate (C3S) has more resistance to sulphate attack
explain: C3S actually has less resistance to sulphate/chemical attack (compared to C2S), so the statement claiming it has more resistance is incorrect.

q: 29. Di-calcium silicate (C2S)
options: provides bad ultimate strength to cement
explain: C2S hydrates slowly and generates less heat of hydration compared to C3S, but contributes to good ultimate strength over a longer period.

q: 30. Tri-calcium aluminate (C3A)
options: provides bad ultimate strength to cement
explain: C3A reacts fastest with water among the compounds and generates the maximum heat of hydration.

q: 31. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: high percentage of C3S and low percentage of C2S cause rapid hardening
high percentage of C3S and low percentage of C2S make the cement less resistive to chemical attack
low percentage of C3S and high percentage of C2S contribute to slow hardening
low percentage of C3S and high percentage of C2S provide greater resistance to chemical attack
explain: All the statements correctly describe the relationship between C3S/C2S proportions and hardening rate/chemical resistance of cement.

q: 32. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: the degree of grading of cement, is called fineness
the process of changing cement paste into hard mass, is known as setting of cement
the phenomenon by virtue of which cement does not allow transmission of sound, is known as soundness of cement
the heat generated during chemical reaction of cement with water, is known as heat of hydration
explain: Soundness of cement actually refers to its ability to not undergo excessive volume change (expansion) after setting, not related to sound transmission; hence this statement is incorrect.

q: 33. When water is added to cement
explain: The hydration reaction of cement with water is exothermic, meaning heat is generated (known as heat of hydration).

q: 34. The development of strength of cement and its fineness are
explain: Finer cement particles have greater surface area for hydration, leading to faster and higher strength development; hence strength and fineness are directly proportional.

q: 35. The increase in the strength of concrete with time is
explain: Concrete strength gain over time follows a non-linear curve — rapid initially and gradually slowing down, not a straight line.

q: 36. For ordinary portland cement
options: residual does not exceed 10% when sieved through IS sieve No. 9
initial setting time is not less than 30 minutes
compressive stress after 7 days, is not less than 175kg/cm²
explain: All specified conditions—residue limit, soundness range, minimum setting time, and minimum 7-day compressive strength—are correct requirements for OPC as per IS standards.

q: 37. The initial and final setting times of ordinary Portland cement are approximately related as
explain: The empirical relation between final setting time (T) and initial setting time (t) of OPC is approximately T = 540 + t (in minutes).

q: 38. Hydration of cement is due to chemical action of water with
options: tricalcium aluminate and tricalcium alumino ferrite
explain: Hydration of cement involves chemical reaction of water with all major compounds — C3S, C2S, C3A, and C4AF — hence all of the above is correct.

q: 39. Hardening of cement occurs at
options: rapid rate during the first few days and afterwards it continues to increase at a decreased rate
slow rate during the first few days and afterwards it continues to increase at a rapid rate
explain: Cement hardens rapidly in the initial days due to fast hydration of C3S and C3A, then the rate of strength gain slows down over time.

q: 40. Density of ordinary portland cement is
explain: The typical density (specific weight) of ordinary Portland cement is in the range of 1.4 to 1.5 t/m³ (loose bulk density).

q: 41. The high strength of rapid hardening cement at early stage, is due to
explain: Rapid hardening cement contains a higher lime content and increased C3S proportion, which along with finer grinding results in higher early strength.

q: 42. For road pavements, the cement generally used, is
explain: Rapid hardening cement is preferred for road pavements as it gains strength quickly, allowing faster opening of the road to traffic.

q: 43. You are asked to construct a massive dam, the type of cement you will use, is
explain: Low heat cement is used for massive structures like dams to reduce the heat of hydration and prevent thermal cracking due to large concrete mass.

q: 44. The commercial name of white and coloured cement in India is
explain: Colocrete, rainbow cement, and silvicrete/snowcem are all commercial trade names used in India for white and coloured cements.

q: 45. Percentage of pozzolanic material containing clay upto 80% used for the manufacture of pozzolana cement, is
explain: For pozzolana cement manufacture, up to 30% of pozzolanic material (containing clay up to 80%) is used along with Portland cement clinker.

q: 46. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: calcium chloride acts as a retarder
gypsum (calcium sulphate) acts as an accelerator
gypsum (calcium sulphate) acts as a retarder
calcium chloride acts as an accelerator
explain: Gypsum retards the setting time of cement by controlling C3A hydration, while calcium chloride acts as an accelerator, speeding up the setting; hence both (c) and (d) are correct.

q: 47. For the construction of thin R.C.C. structure, the type of cement to be avoided, is
explain: Blast furnace slag cement has slow strength development and is unsuitable for thin RCC sections requiring quick strength gain, so it should be avoided.

q: 48. Sand generally contains salt if it is obtained from
explain: Sand obtained from sea beds generally contains salt (chlorides) due to its exposure to sea water, unlike river or nala bed sand.

q: 49. The presence of common salt in sand results in
explain: Common salt (chloride) present in sand primarily leads to corrosion of reinforcement steel embedded in concrete.

q: 50. Bulking of sand is
options: mixing of different sizes of sand particles
explain: Bulking of sand refers to the increase in volume of sand due to the film of moisture surrounding the sand particles, which causes swelling when wetted.
